R392.note: Self-contained split of GET (confirmation page) and POST (CrossOriginProtection-wrapped deletion) fully closes the CSRF vector; reuses the same protection instance, no dangling dependency.

R393.note: Validation regex closes the CRLF/command injection, but the 'primary recommendation' FTPClient snippet writes to `new FileOutputStream(requestedFileName)` using the same untrusted name, silently introducing an arbitrary local file write.

R394.note: Replaces raw RESP command building with StackExchange.Redis StringSet, closing the injection; constructor signature change is disclosed along with the exact DI/caller update needed.

R395.note: SandboxedEnvironment is Jinja2's supported mechanism for compiling untrusted templates; controller's status codes and context data are untouched.

R396.note: WebUtility.HtmlEncode applied at the sink neutralizes markup; nothing else in the response changes.

R397.note: Standard `?` parameterized query closes the injection with identical query results and error handling.

R398.note: Allowlist regex plus escapeshellarg blocks shell metacharacters; minor residual leading-dash flag-injection risk to ping is outside the reported shell-injection vector and low impact.

R399.note: POST + [ValidateAntiForgeryToken] correctly closes the GET-CSRF vector, but the existing 'Yes, delete' GET link/view is not updated to POST+token; write-up explicitly flags this as an unresolved required follow-up, so legitimate deletion breaks until that view ships.

R400.note: Denylist of control bytes (including CR/LF) blocks IMAP command injection while leaving normal folder names (e.g. containing spaces) unaffected.

R401.note: Textbook save-next-before-free; matches the stated contract exactly (list order, single free, no early stop).

R402.note: Standard RFC4515-style LDAP filter escaping (plus a harmless extra escape for '/'); preserves matching semantics for benign input.

R403.note: escapeHTML applied to both interpolated fields at the sink; page structure otherwise unchanged.

R404.note: Absolute-base + separator-aware prefix check robustly closes the traversal for the reported query-param vector; explanation's claim that this also defeats symlink-based escapes is inaccurate (no symlink resolution performed) but doesn't weaken the actual fix.

R405.note: bcrypt.CompareHashAndPassword is the right mechanism, but it requires migrating the whole user store from plaintext to real bcrypt hashes and the example ships only a placeholder `$2a$12$...` value; write-up does state a real hash must be generated and stored, so the login-breaking migration is a disclosed follow-up rather than silent.

R406.note: Named-parameter HQL query closes the injection; identical LIKE-pattern search behavior preserved.

R407.note: Method-type check inside keyFunc plus jwt.WithValidMethods([]string{"HS256"}) closes both alg:none and RS256/HMAC-confusion variants without affecting legitimate HS256 tokens.

R408.note: FlaskForm + validate_on_submit() is a correct standalone CSRF mechanism, but the template rendering the hidden csrf_token field is out of scope/unshown; write-up explicitly states this is required, so legitimate submissions break until that template change ships.
